ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (BodySlam.cs:25-28) == cost 1 / ATTACK / COMMON / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `CalculationBaseVar(0m)` + `ExtraDamageVar(1m)` + `CalculatedDamageVar(ValueProp.Move).WithMultiplier((card, _) => card.Owner.Creature.Block)` (BodySlam.cs:16-21). `CalculatedVar.Calculate` is `base + extra * multiplier` (CalculatedVar.cs:62-71), i.e. `0 + 1 * Block` == the sim's `return ctx.player.block`. This is precisely the CalculationBase-0 / Extra-1 idiom the C# doc comment prescribes for entirely dynamic cards (CalculatedDamageVar.cs class comment, which names BodySlam), so the sim's direct read is the same value. Move without Unpowered -> powered on both sides.

OnPlay.rationale: `DamageCmd.Attack(DynamicVars.CalculatedDamage).FromCard(this).Targeting(cardPlay.Target)` (BodySlam.cs:33-35) == `DamageCmd.deal(ctx.hooks, target, self.calc_damage(ctx, target), dealer=ctx.player, card=self)`. The block is read at play time on both sides, so block gained earlier in the same turn counts. Presentation, folded in: WithHitFx and the static Block hover tip (BodySlam.cs:23).

OnUpgrade.rationale: `EnergyCost.UpgradeBy(-1)` (BodySlam.cs:40) == `self._energy_cost = max(0, self._energy_cost - 1)` (1 -> 0). The damage formula is unchanged by the upgrade on both sides -- upgraded values checked.

guards.what: the multiplier reads the OWNER's block, not the target's (BodySlam.cs:20)
guards.rationale: `card.Owner.Creature.Block` == `ctx.player.block`. Single-player throughout, so no owner ambiguity.

guards.what: block is resolved BEFORE the attack pipeline runs, so retaliation during the same attack cannot shrink it
guards.rationale: The sim evaluates `calc_damage` in the argument list of the single `DamageCmd.deal` call, exactly as C# resolves the DynamicVar before Execute. Same value on both sides.
